title: Inspect users and their groups
goal: Separate account database information from a running process's identity.
challenge: Create one locked disposable ll-u1 account using the supplied setup. Identify its UID, primary/supplementary groups, home and shell; compare a process running as it with the account database. Leave learner and system accounts unchanged.

steps.command: ! getent passwd ll-u1 && ! getent group ll-u1 && test ! -e /home/ll-u1 && sudo useradd -m -U -s /bin/bash ll-u1
steps.explanation: Fail closed if this disposable name or home exists. -m creates a home from /etc/skel; -U creates a primary group; no password is set.
steps.expected: Fresh account ll-u1, same-named primary group, home and Bash shell. A nonzero status/collision means stop setup.

steps.command: id; id ll-u1; getent passwd ll-u1; getent group ll-u1
steps.explanation: id without a name describes this process; id with a name queries account membership. /etc/passwd contains account metadata, not plaintext passwords.
steps.expected: learner process differs from ll-u1; ll-u1 primary group/home/Bash visible.

steps.command: sudo runuser -u ll-u1 -- id; sudo passwd -S ll-u1
steps.explanation: Run a real command under the new identity. L means password locked, not that root cannot launch commands as that user.
steps.expected: UID and GID belong to ll-u1; status L. No password/login success is claimed.

steps.command: getent passwd ll-service; getent group ll-service
steps.explanation: Inspect the existing service account read-only. Service identities need not have interactive shells.
steps.expected: ll-service uses nologin. No service/learner metadata was edited.

hints: Compare UID/GID numbers and names, rather than relying on a shell prompt.
The group record need not list a user whose membership comes from their primary GID.
Run id under the intended identity to distinguish database lookup from current credentials.
review: Retain ll-u1 account metadata and the two id outputs; explain primary versus supplementary group.
Show ll-u1 locked status without displaying shadow entries or setting credentials.
coverage: LPIC-1 107.1 account/group database inspection. Partial coverage; original material, self-review only. No automatic assessment or full LPIC preparation.
